llm_extracted_info.main_contributions: The paper introduces Transformer-VQ, a decoder-only transformer that computes softmax-based dense self-attention in linear time with respect to sequence length. Its key innovations are vector-quantized keys and a novel caching mechanism, which allow for efficient attention. Transformer-VQ demonstrates highly competitive quality on long-context autoregressive modeling benchmarks, achieving 0.99 bpb on Enwik8, 26.6 ppl on PG-19, and 3.16 bpb on ImageNet64. It also significantly improves speed, being over 3x faster than comparable quadratic-time transformers at sequence length 8k, over 12x faster at 32k, and scalable to 131k sequences with similar throughput.
llm_extracted_info.methodology: Transformer-VQ achieves linear-time dense self-attention through vector-quantized keys, localized positional biases, and a compressive cache. It utilizes a Vector-Quantized Self-Attention (VQAttn) mechanism, which is applied to a Gated Attention Unit (GAU) design. Vector quantization employs a straight-through gradient estimator for backpropagation, and codebooks are updated using EMA-smoothed k-means. The core of the linear-time computation is a block-level recurrence relation for the product WV (attention weights times values), which is presented for both element-wise and row-wise softmax nonlinearities. For numerical stability, the implementation stores running means of value vectors assigned to shortcodes instead of sums, moving the logarithm of counts inside exponentials.
llm_extracted_info.experimental_setup: Experiments were conducted using Jax and Flax, trained on TPU v3 pod slices. Performance was benchmarked against unquantized quadratic-time full attention baselines. Models with roughly 190M and 1.3B parameters were evaluated. Ablation studies investigated codebook size (S=256, 512, 1024) and the importance of the compressive cache on Enwik8. Throughput comparisons were made for various sequence lengths (2048 to 131072) and head types (MHA, MQA, SHGA) using serial scan, matmul, and associative scan reduction methods. Quantitative results were presented on Enwik8 (byte-level language modeling), PG-19 (open-vocabulary language modeling), and ImageNet64 (autoregressive density estimation), reporting bits-per-byte (BPB) and word-level perplexity (WLP). Hyperparameters included specific batch sizes, sequence lengths, model dimensions, dropout rates, and optimizers (AdamW, Adafactor). Generated samples were qualitatively analyzed using nucleus sampling.
llm_extracted_info.limitations: The model faces overfitting issues on the Enwik8 dataset, and due to the compressive cache mechanism, i.i.d. attention dropout was not feasible. While competitive, Transformer-VQ falls short of state-of-the-art results on Enwik8 compared to some works using complex recurrence or forgetting mechanisms. The ImageNet64 results use a newer variant of the dataset, which cannot be directly compared with baselines using an earlier variant, introducing ambiguity in reported state-of-the-art claims for that dataset. The paper also notes that while FLASH, a prior method, uses a similar general strategy for computing un-normalized softmax and its denominator, it has known weaknesses in stability that Transformer-VQ addresses.
llm_extracted_info.future_research_directions: Future work includes conducting formal scaling laws to better understand the model's behavior with increasing size, developing even larger models, and porting the implementation to lower-level frameworks such as Pallas, Triton, or CUDA for further optimization and performance gains.

--sequence_len (int): Sequence length T.
--update_len (int): Update length LK.
--block_len (int): Block length L.
--mem_len (int): Band length M.
--grad_thru_cache (int): Backprop through cache (0/1).
--agg_cache (int): Include aggregated cache (0/1).

--param_dtype (choices: bfloat16, float32): Dtype for parameters.
--dtype (choices: bfloat16, float32): Dtype for computation.
--d_model (int): Model width.
--d_k (int): Key width.
--d_v (int): Value width.
--d_ff (int): Fan-out width, if using MLPs (default: 0).
--n_head (int): Number of attention heads.
--n_code (int): Number of codes per head.
--n_layer (int): Number of transformer layers (two GAU each).
